title: Introduce cross-tenant noise injector and anchored replay runner for reproducible interference experiments
author: Leah Kim
description:
Motivation: reproducing cross-tenant interference reliably has been a recurring blocker for debugging tail latency regressions. Randomized noise injection and ad-hoc replay scripts made experiments hard to reproduce across runs and clusters. This PR adds two complementary pieces: (1) a configurable cross-tenant noise injector that can playback a small 'background traffic' trace with deterministic seeding and time-anchoring, and (2) an anchored replay runner that ties foreground request traces to fixed wall-clock anchors so repeated runs are bit-for-bit comparable.

What this PR does (high level):
- Implements a lightweight noise model with pluggable distributions (poisson, bursty, correlated-bursts) and an explicit RNG-seed parameter for reproducibility.
- Adds an "anchor" mechanism: a foreground trace is annotated with anchor timestamps; the runner aligns trace playback to those anchors so warmup/coldstart windows and KV-cache priming are deterministic.
- Introduces a compact exporter (CSV + optional parquet metadata header) that records per-request anchor ids, injected-noise-tags, latency p50/p95/p99, and kernel attribution hints to streamline downstream delta-analysis.
- Adds runtime markers in the runner to expose prefetched primer events to perf collectors (small header in runtime_markers.h and emitted markers in critical path).
- Integrates with existing perf CI: a new perf-suite job wiring leverages the anchored runner for nightly regression baselines.

Why this is different: many previous runners either randomized noise or relied on wall-clock-only replays; combining anchored timestamps + deterministic seeds removes two big sources of nondeterminism (schedule jitter and PRNG variance) and lets us produce reproducible diffable telemetry.

review_thread: Owen Price (2026-02-11): Nice work. Two questions: (1) how do we ensure the RNG seed doesn't collide across parallel runners? Should seeds be namespaced by runner-id? (2) The markers in runtime_markers.h look fine, but can we make the emission a no-op behind a build flag to avoid perf noise in production?

Leah Kim (2026-02-11): Reply: good points. Seeds are namespaced by cluster_id + runner_id; see noise_model.py:SeedNamespace. I'll add a note to docs. Marker emission is gated behind RUNTIME_MARKERS_ENABLED; runtime default is off.

Sana Patel (2026-02-12): Tests look solid but I hit a flaky CI failure on macOS for parquet optional dependency (file lock on writer). Could we retry with the dependency gated further and add a temp file strategy?
Leah Kim (2026-02-12): Reply: added temp-file write/resilient-flush in compact_exporter and re-ran tests. CI macOS job now passes.
Miguel Alvarez (2026-02-13): Approve after small nits fixed in docs and adding example noise_profile. Marking approval.
